Dungeon Master Assistant

What this tool will not do. It will not decide for you — the DMG defers to the DM about 185 times, and what a failure means (p.242), whether to roll at all (p.236) and whether a monster is fun (p.275) are not gaps to close. It will not print a number it cannot cite, and it will not fill a hole in its own rules data: an unreadable table cell stays an explicit gap.
State lives in this browser (localStorage), autosaved on every action — Export for a portable copy, Import to move it. The Player View panel is the disclosure wall: per fact, opt-in, DM's call.

Licence. Content is tagged on the Rules tab, and the tag is not decorative: a SRD-CC-BY entry records the full-text search that proved it is in the open document. Portions of the rules content here are used under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License, based on material from the System Reference Document 5.1 by Wizards of the Coast LLC, available at https://media.wizards.com/2023/downloads/dnd/SRD_CC_v5.1.pdf, used under the terms of that licence. Entries tagged proprietary came from books that grant no redistribution rights — this build is for your own table, not for publishing. Entries tagged design are this tool's own models and cite no page. This tool is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Wizards of the Coast.

The Monster Manual index (Phase 3). It is a pointer — a name, a page, the challenge rating where the parse is confident, and at most two short lines — into a book this build's owner already owns. It is DM-view only, excluded from the Player View, the recap, the briefing card, the rules-answer text and any paste-able prompt, and a build made with --no-dm-only leaves it out entirely so the artifact can be shared.

The optional model adapter (Phase 4). Every Phase 4 screen works offline and deterministically: the sentences come from the transcribed phrase banks and tables, and a state change the bank cannot phrase is refused rather than invented. The BYO-model adapter is a separate opt-in the DM flips at the table. This artifact ships with it off, with no service address typed and no key of any kind — the saved state has no field that could hold one, which is the same argument the Monster Manual index makes about holding no stat block. A build gate counts the URLs in this file and finds only the licence link above, so “offline by default” is a checked property of the file you forward to a friend, not a promise in a README.

The review gate (Phase 5). Nothing a delegated die decides is true for your campaign until you say so. Every roll, vignette line, loyalty change and scene summary lands in delegated.reviewQueue with decision: null, and only a row in delegated.approvals — which must name a ledger row that already exists, and which can be revoked — attaches it to your campaign. No approval writes coin, an item, a memory note or a level of its own: the purse is Phase 1’s, the memory is Phase 2’s, and what the gate records is that the content was reviewed. The side tier is DM-side by default (visibility.delegated is false in a new campaign and in a migrated one); opened, the one thing that reaches a player surface is an approved, mechanically-silent vignette sentence, and the count of what was withheld is written in words because a digit on that tab is what the build gate searches for. Phase 5 ships no second transport: it calls the Phase 4 adapter rather than forking one, its preferences hold no key and no service address, and there is no switch in this build that posts anything to your campaign automatically. Where the scan destroyed a table — the fourteen garrison rows are still unrecoverable and still refused — the panel shows the wreckage and refuses; where a cost belongs to a book this build does not have — a lifestyle, a stronghold’s upkeep — it prints the deferral instead of a number. (The carousing jail band was re-read off the printed page in Phase 6.1, so it now prints its minimum; the repair ledger beside it says what it used to say and how that was found.)

The repair tier and the generator (Phase 6). The reference material this build ships is never rewritten by using it: a fix on the Editing tab is a patch stored in your campaign, naming the file, the row and the path it replaces, with the shipped value kept as its before — and revoking the patch puts the book back. A patch may not reach a cite, a source or a licence field at any depth: if a citation looks wrong, the scan that made it is what needs fixing. And a character the generator produced is not a member of your party until you send it to the Roster and press Add — the sheet waits on the Characters tab under a name you typed, and deleting that sheet never deletes a character. The generator itself is a file this DM supplied and this build embeds: it runs in a frame sandboxed to scripting and its own print control, its document is decoded out of this artifact rather than fetched, it asks the network for nothing, and a build made with --no-dm-only leaves that file out entirely.
